deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 4, 'Topos canoniques associés à une stratification globale', part A, 'Images inverses générales'. A global stratification of X is a locally finite family (X_i), i in a poset I, of closed subsets. It satisfies four conditions: X_i is contained in X_j whenever i ≤ j; the X_i cover X; and X_i ∩ X_j is the union of the X_k with k ≤ i, j. For any X' → X, the pulled-back family X'_i = X_i ×_X X' satisfies the same axioms. The associated objects X_{Δ_r}, X*_{Δ_r} and the punctured X_{Δ_r} pull back as well (previous page, (3)).

This page makes four points.

(i) NB. The tubular neighbourhoods were so far only treated for X' open in X. To allow pullbacks along more general maps, one should probably NOT require the strata X_i (or the open strata X_i*) to be non-empty. Nor should one require I → 𝔉(X) to be an order embedding into the closed subsets. Pullback can kill strata or identify them.

(ii) For X' → X a proper local immersion (explicitly not just an open immersion), the formation of tubular neighbourhoods and of the associated partitions commutes with inverse image.

(iii) For i < j, R'_{ij} = R_{ij} ×_X X' and S'_{ij} = S_{ij} ×_X X'. These are the auxiliary data, apparently the 'rideaux' and partition pieces of the tube of X_i in X_j. This holds with no hypothesis on X' → X.

(iv) Hence, for a proper local immersion, there are isomorphisms (5): V'_{ij} ≃ V_{ij} ×_X X' (i ≤ j) and V'*_{ij} ≃ V*_{ij} ×_X X'. The next page extends this to the higher tubes V~_{i,n}. It concludes that the tubular-neighbourhood theorems (p. 22) are local on X.

Margin: there is an underlying formal property, the compatibility of tubular neighbourhoods and partitions with inverse images, to be isolated (cf. 'X convenable').

The page serves the general programme of building canonical topoi and 'dévissage' structures from a stratification, in a tame-topology setting. That programme is announced in Esquisse §5.
errors: No real error. The claim that (5) holds for proper local immersions is plausible: a local immersion pulls neighbourhoods back to neighbourhoods. Properness is presumably needed so that the tube's closure and retraction properties survive. The page gives no proof.
Equation (5) as written puts a star on the first line too; by context the first line should be the unstarred V'_{ij} ≃ V_{ij} ×_X X'.
Dropping non-emptiness and injectivity of I → 𝔉(X) is necessary for (2) to hold. The text correctly notices this (pullback can empty strata or make them coincide).

ideas.what: Stability of a poset-indexed closed stratification under arbitrary base change, requiring dropping non-emptiness and injectivity of strata
ideas.modern_name: pullback of poset-stratified spaces (stratifications as continuous maps X → I with Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; formalized e.g. in Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses stratified structures informally

ideas.what: Compatibility of tubular neighbourhoods (and the induced partitions) with pullback along proper local immersions; locality of tube theorems on X
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of control data / tubular systems under stratified pullback
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (Mather 1970); Quinn's homotopically stratified sets (1988)

ideas.what: Call to isolate an abstract 'formal property' of compatibility between tubes and partitions
ideas.modern_name: axiomatization of tubular/link structures (homotopy links, exit-path data)

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags an underlying formal property, the compatibility of tubular neighbourhoods with partitions under inverse image, to be extracted. This is a programme to axiomatize the tube structure functorially, in the spirit later realized via homotopy links and exit paths. It is only a minor unfinished note.
missed.quote: Il y a ici une propriété formelle sous-jacente ... qu'il faudra dégager (cf. X convenable !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only historical: it shows that Grothendieck sought a functorial, base-change-stable formulation of tube data in 1981. That predates Quinn's homotopy-link approach, which achieved something similar. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine technical remarks on base change of stratifications and tubular neighbourhoods within Grothendieck's tame-topology notes. They are historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'topos stratifié' programme, but mathematically standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Nous n'avons défini[?] ces voisinages tubulaires que dans le cas où X' est un ouvert de X'.
Line 4 should read '...qu'il convenait peut-être de ne pas supposer les X_i ou les X_i* non vides': the logic requires a negation.
'I ↪ 𝔖(X)' is more likely 'I ↪ 𝔉(X)', the set of closed subsets (fraktur F).
'Lorsque X'→X est une immersion locale propre (mais pas [nécessairement] une immersion ouverte !)': 'propre' is inserted above, and 'Question' is struck and replaced by 'mais pas'.
In (5), the first line should be V'_{i,j} (no star) for i ≤ j.
Margin is roughly: 'Il y a ici une propriété formelle sous-jacente, de compatibilité des voisinages tubulaires et des partitions, qu'il faudra dégager (cf. X convenable !)'.
